newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore key share index hits 28-month low.
newsitem.headline: Singapore key share index hits 28-month low.

text.p: Singapore's key Straits Times Industrials Index hit 1,979.67 in late afternoon trading on Friday, its lowest level in 28 months.
Dealers attributed the fall to bearish technicals and to a lack of confidence in the Singapore market, which was keeping major funds away.
"There are no fresh leads in Singapore. Nothing good in the near term to look forward to. Cerebos's poor interim results just triggered the selling," said a dealer with a local broking house.

Earlier this week, index-linked food-related Cerebos disappointed with flat earnings of S$47.01 million for the six months ended March 31, 1997 against expectations of double digit growth. It also warned of a tougher second half.
Cerebos' disappointing earnings prompted investors to sell shares in soft-drink company Fraser & Neave, another index-linked stock, ahead of its results due later on Friday.
At 0815 GMT, the index was at 1,979.99, down 10.69 points.
Some dealers said they expected the index to drift to around 1,900 by end of June given the lack of encouraging news.
"There is no turnaround seen in the major shipyards and some sectors in the economy," one broker said.
Another dealer said, however, a sparkle in property or bank stocks could lend some support to the otherwise dismal market. -- Singapore newsroom (65 8703083)
